newsitem.title: GERMANY: WestLB says won't withdraw Iran loan.
newsitem.headline: WestLB says won't withdraw Iran loan.

text.p: German bank WestLB on Monday refused to withdraw a loan it granted to Iran's Offshore Engineering and Construction Company despite being warned by a U.S. senator that the deal would violate U.S. law.
A WestLB spokesman said the bank was not breaching any laws because trade finance deals were not covered by the 1996 Iran Libya Sanctions Act (ILSA).
"We are acting fully in line with the law," the spokesman said.
WestLB -- Westdeutsche Landesbank Girozentrale -- belongs to a bank consortium that has lent the state-owned Iranian company $90 million. WestLB's share of the loan is $40 million.
The loan will be used to finance the supply of machinery and technical equipment by German, French and Belgian exporters to develop the Souroush oil field, the WestLB spokesman said.
In a letter sent last week to WestLB chief Friedel Neuber, New York Republican Senator Al D'Amato said the deal was a clear violation of ILSA.
D'Amato was a key author of the legislation, which imposes U.S. sanctions on any company that invests $40 million or more in a 12-month period in the petroleum sectors of Iran or Libya.

D'Amato said the scheme would be nothing more than an effort to wilfully circumvent ILSA and that any business deal that provided Iran with hard currency to develop its energy sector was regarded as a direct threat to U.S. national security.
He also said that if WestLB went ahead with the loan it would become a "pariah company known for supporting rogue states".
